fields.summary: Autonomous plan run on change set 01M6W4K (Scheduled triggers). No owner took part: the planner raised two batches of questions and the arbiter answered each with a Decision worded (assumed, would have escalated). Facts from the code: rhiza.toml is the root's machine-wide config (internal/rootcfg), not committed in any repo and shared by several projects; workflow dispatch (01M6VY7G, accepted, not yet built) moved its rules to a committed .rhiza/dispatch.toml for that reason and serves milestone-25; every run today needs a change set and its worktree (RunStartRequest.Change, internal/api/run.go); rhiza health reports fixed parts (internal/api/health.go); the repo has no .rhiza/policy.toml, so backlog work builds after milestone work. Settled in scheduled-triggers-shape: the change set serves milestone-25; [[schedules]] live in .rhiza/dispatch.toml with name, every or cron, workflow or command; a scheduled run has no change set, runs on the main checkout, records trigger schedule and the schedule's name, and acts on the model only through existing paths such as queuing requests; scheduled runs share maxRuns, a due slot waits for a free slot and counts as one firing; per schedule only catch_up (once or skip) and overlap (skip or queue) are overridable. Settled in scheduled-run-readonly-cron-health: read-only is a documented convention, never a fence, with a warning when a run changed the main checkout's branch, HEAD or tracked files; cron is five-field with names, macros and CRON_TZ, local time by default, classic day-field OR and DST rules; every is a Go duration of at least 1m aligned to epoch multiples in UTC; health gains a schedules part per project with schedules, warn at worst. Also found: rhiza change show fails on this change set with 'not canonical' because of the known @-reference re-encoding bug, already tracked by draft change set 01M6VYTS (Fix change show HTML escape).
fields.title: Scheduled triggers plan, autonomous run with the arbiter
